text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for type 2 diabetes include lifestyle adjustments, oral and injectable medications, and monitoring tools.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle adjustments, oral and injectable medications, and monitoring tools

list.snippet: Healthy diet: Eat a balanced meal plan rich in non-starchy vegetables, lean proteins, and complex carbohydrates with guidance from the Cleveland Clinic.
Physical activity: Exercise regularly, such as brisk walking or resistance training, to help your body use insulin efficiently.
Weight management: Lose a modest amount of excess weight to significantly improve blood sugar control.
Metformin: Prescribed most often as the first-line oral medication to decrease liver glucose production and improve insulin sensitivity.
Other oral drugs: Options include sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones (TZDs), and DPP-4 or SGLT2 inhibitors to boost insulin or manage glucose excretion.
Injectable therapies: GLP-1 receptor agonists (or dual GLP-1/GIP agonists) help lower blood sugar and support weight loss.
Insulin therapy: Used when oral or other injectables are not enough to reach target blood glucose levels.
Blood sugar tracking: Use traditional finger-prick meters or continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) to track how food, activity, and medicine affect your glucose.
